questions: Compared with iteration 1 (lead 0.03 m, otherwise identical), does the 0.04 m lead raise s-bend progress above 0.26 and raise or hold oval progress at or above 0.47?
Does max_error fall toward or below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend? Where does the first off-track event occur (track, bend, progress, time)? Use per-step telemetry if available.
Does steering_oscillation stay near the iteration-1 level of about 0.28, or does the longer look-ahead make the signal lag and overshoot?
Does the line-loss count change on the slalom, particularly on the tightest bends?
Which geometry limit now constrains the controller most: sensor lead, sensor spread, wheel_track or mass?

intent: Single-variable test of sensor lead. Keep the iteration-1 design (5 sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 with 0.025 m spacing, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.10, wheel_radius 0.035, mass 0.6, body 0.14 x 0.10) and move the sensor row from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.04 m. Expected: s-bend and oval progress at or above the iteration-1 values, max_error at or below 0.06 m, and fewer off-track endings than iteration 1.
learning: Iteration 5 showed that a shorter lead (0.02 m) hurt progress and s-bend performance, so look-ahead is valuable. This iteration tests the other side of the lead, 0.04 m, with everything else as in iteration 1. If s-bend and oval progress both rise, the next step is to refine the lead between 0.04 and 0.05 m or to check whether the excursions are now on the slalom. If oscillation rises sharply or line loss increases, the lead optimum is near 0.03 m and the next geometry lever is wheel_track (0.09 to 0.10 m) or mass.
rationale:
Scores so far are 52.3, 114.4 (iteration 1, best), 65.7, 102.8, 110.2 and 91.8. Every run in every iteration ended off track with zero finishes. Max error sits at 0.061 to 0.068 m, just over the 0.06 m off-track limit, while RMS error stays at 0.023 to 0.031 m. The robot tracks well until a single excursion takes it past the edge, so the lever is how it responds to excursions.

Body width cannot help. The limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and even at 0.18 m that is 0.0575 m, so the 0.06 m floor governs. Sensor-array changes have not beaten iteration 1: 7 sensors at 16 mm cut oval progress to 0.23, and 5 sensors at 8 mm gave 0.41. Drivetrain changes in iteration 4 (wheel_radius 0.04, mass 0.5, body_length 0.12) gave no gain, with oscillation up to 0.33.

The sensor lead is the one geometry variable I have isolated only partly. Lead 0.02 m (iteration 5) against 0.03 m (iteration 1), with everything else equal, was worse: score 91.8 against 114.4, s-bend progress 0.11 against 0.26, and oval progress 0.44 against 0.47. Oscillation fell, so the shorter lead appears to lose look-ahead on bends. That suggests more look-ahead helps. Iteration 0 used 0.05 m, but it was confounded with other changes and scored low, so the optimum is probably between 0.03 and 0.05 m.

Decision: keep the iteration-1 design exactly, and change only the sensor lead from 0.03 m to 0.04 m. This is a single-variable test on the lever that the iteration-5 result points at. Expected result: s-bend progress rises above 0.26, oval progress stays at or above 0.47, and max_error falls toward or below 0.06 m. Risk: the longer look-ahead may lag on the tightest bends and push max_error or line-loss events up on the slalom.
